translationRepairs: Gao Anagujin was a master of flattery.
Gao Anagujin was a native of Shanwu.
善無人也 is the standard native-place formula naming Shanwu (善無), not a claim that he was skilled at flattery.
Gao Anagujin was skilled at ingratiation.
Gao Anagujin was a native of Shanwu.
善無人也 identifies Gao Anagujin as a man of Shanwu; “skilled at ingratiation” misreads 善無 as a verb phrase.
The Later Lord had Attendant Hulu Xiaoxiao investigate; Xiaoxiao said, "This man speaks falsely."
The Later Lord had Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing investigate; Xiaoqing said, "This man speaks falsely."
斛律孝卿 is Hulu Xiaoqing (孝卿); Xiaoxiao is a wrong reading of the given name.
The Later Lord ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoxiao to investigate; Xiaoxiao said, "This man speaks falsely."
The Later Lord ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoqing to investigate; Xiaoqing said, "This man speaks falsely."
孝卿 romanizes as Xiaoqing, not Xiaoxiao; the proposed literal correctly restores the name while leaving the rest intact.
Sent to build a fortress at Liyang on the river, he said, "In a pinch we can hold this and play king of Kucha; life is brief—why not enjoy it?"

Later the emperor sent him to build a fortress at Liyang on the river and said, "In a pinch we can hold this and play at being princes of Kucha; human life is but a sojourn—one should only seek pleasure; why grieve?"

後帝使…曰 makes the emperor the speaker, so the original wrongfully attributes the speech to Han Feng; the proposed after fixes attribution but is awkward (“how much more that human life is a lodging”), so the idiomatic wording is revised for natural English while keeping the emperor as speaker and the fuller sense of 人生如寄…何因愁為.
